# Managed-retail reference: ~$2.50/M output, ~$0.50/M input, 262K ctx, ~300 tok/s single-stream.
# VERDICT (cost, MEASURED): single TP4 replica at full-batch ~$6.00-6.10/M output, 2.4x the ~$2.50/M retail reference.
#   Retail prices at scale-amortized multi-tenant batching + reserved/owned hardware; our number is raw spot with zero margin.
# VERDICT (latency, MEASURED): single-stream decode 297.7 tok/s ESSENTIALLY MATCHES the 300 tok/s reference (0.99x); first-run SGLang missed (177).
# 2-REPLICA HEADROOM (PROJECTED, NOT MEASURED): the benchmark used only 4 of 8 GPUs (TP4). A second independent TP4
#   replica fits on GPUs 4-7 (each replica used ~171/183 GB/GPU; replicas don't share GPUs). It does NOT raise single-stream
#   speed (per-request latency is unchanged - a replica serves *different* requests), but ~doubles aggregate throughput at
#   the SAME instance cost, halving $/M:
#     - ideal 2.0x scaling:    ~3766 tok/s -> ~$2.99/M (1.20x retail) - essentially infra-level parity (our $ has no margin).
#     - realistic 1.8x (NVSwitch contention): ~3389 tok/s -> ~$3.33/M (1.33x retail).
#   Caveat: projection assumes linear/near-linear replica scaling; not validated on hardware (node already torn down).
#   Alternative: a single TP8 replica across all 8 GPUs would also use the idle GPUs - likely better single-stream latency
#   (fewer effective decode hops) but $/M stays ~flat; 2x TP4 maximizes aggregate throughput/$ instead.
